order: Draw the synthetic corpus for the misroute-recovery study and pre-register its gates. Build 24 items, 13 misroutes and 11 correctly routed, whose true classes are an authorial fact of construction, covering both reserved edges — the persisted-generated-output horn, with an accepted control and a baited misroute, and the values-only horn likewise. Register three gates, all of them fixed before any model runs: every constructed misroute must be caught by the receiving seat's charter filter. No misroute may cross a mandatory review, tier or third-stage gate, with gate relevance computed mechanically from the router's own review-policy and required-question fields under assigned versus true class. Reclassification must stay within one hop at the 95th percentile. Keep one-shot classifier agreement, false bounces and recommended-class accuracy as non-gating telemetry. Add a mechanical scorer that exits zero or one on the gates, running recovery through the router's reclassification path.
claims: The corpus and the mechanical scorer are in place and the gates were registered ahead of any model pass. The scorer reports all three passing, with thirteen of thirteen constructed misroutes caught, four gate-relevant misroutes crossing none, and tier-borne gates staying identical under both dispatches for every item. The hop count sat at one, at the ninety-fifth percentile, with no escalations. Recovery runs through the router's reclassification path, the telemetry counters are recorded without gating, and the run exits zero.
